answer_text:
# Work Done by Force Field Along a Path

## Setting Up the Problem

The force field is $\mathbf{F} = x^2\mathbf{i} + 2yz\,\mathbf{j} + 4z^2\,\mathbf{k}$, and the particle moves along the straight-line path from $(0,0,0)$ to $(1,1,1)$.

## Parameterizing the Path

I parameterize the straight line from the origin to $(1,1,1)$:

$$x = t,\quad y = t,\quad z = t, \qquad 0 \le t \le 1$$

This gives:

$$dx = dt, \quad dy = dt, \quad dz = dt$$

## Computing the Line Integral

The work is:

$$W = \int_C \mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{r} = \int_0^1 \left(x^2\,\frac{dx}{dt} + 2yz\,\frac{dy}{dt} + 4z^2\,\frac{dz}{dt}\right) dt$$

Substituting $x = y = z = t$:

$$W = \int_0^1 \left(t^2 \cdot 1 + 2(t)(t) \cdot 1 + 4t^2 \cdot 1\right) dt$$

$$W = \int_0^1 \left(t^2 + 2t^2 + 4t^2\right) dt$$

$$W = \int_0^1 7t^2 \, dt$$

## Evaluating

$$W = 7\left[\frac{t^3}{3}\right]_0^1 = 7 \cdot \frac{1}{3} = \frac{7}{3}$$

## Result

$$\boxed{\dfrac{7}{3}}$$
